ORAL ORDER 1] This revision application has been filed by the State of Gujarat through the Public Prosecutor under Section 397 read with Section 401 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ( "the Code")
challenging the order passed below Exhibit 4-J on 28 th September, 2016 in Sessions Case (POCSO)
No. 147 of 2015 by the learned Special Judge (POCSO), City Civil & Sessions Court, Ahmedabad.

2]
The brief facts giving rise to the present revision application are as under:-
2.1] That FIR No. I-C.R.No. 130 of 2015 was filed by the original complainant on 27th July, 2015 at Maninagar Police Station under Sections 363, 366, 376(1), 376(D), 114 and 342 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and under Sections 3, 4, 5(G), 16, 17 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/63/2017 ORDER DATED: 15/02/2024 undefined (POCSO) and Sections 3(2)(5) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,
1989 and after due investigation, a charge sheet came to be filed by the Investigating Officer against 9 accused persons.

Being aggrieved and dissatisfied by the aforesaid order of discharge, the State has filed the present revision application mainly contending that after due investigation, a charge sheet has been filed against all the accused persons and the learned Trial Court has grossly erred in discharging the present respondent from the case.

That, it is on record that the respondent was doing the business of the hotel since last 15 years and when the prosecutrix was taken to the hotel, the identity card and documentary evidences were not asked for and there were many irregularities carried out by the respondent.

That, there was a clear abetment on the part of the respondent by providing the facilities without proper verification of the documents and the allegations against the respondent are very serious and hence the order passed by the learned trial Court is improper and against the evidence collected by the Investigating Officer and hence the order may be set aside.

4] Heard learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the applicant-State and learned advocate Mr. Ashish B Desai for the respondent.
5] Learned Additional Public Prosecutor has vehemently argued that the respondent cannot be discharged in a serious case NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/63/2017 ORDER DATED: 15/02/2024 State Of Gujarat vs Vijaybhai Ramjibhai Soni on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158459410/

sentences.text: However, during investigation, there was enough evidence against the respondent and the charge sheet has been filed.
That, the learned Trial Court has grossly erred in discharging the respondent from a very serious offence and hence the order passed by the learned Trial Court below Exhibit 4-J must be set aside.

6] Learned advocate Mr. Desai for the respondent has submitted that the learned trial Court has considered all the aspects and there was no evidence that the present respondent was in any way connected with the offence and hence the learned trial Court has rightly discharged the respondent from the offence.
That, the learned Trial Court had sifted all the evidences on record properly and there is no illegality or impropriety in the impugned order.

Moreover, learned advocate Mr. Desai submits that the learned trial Court has concluded the trial in Sessions Case (POCSO) No. 147 of 2015 and by a judgment and order dated 05.05.2022, all the accused have been acquitted for all the offences.
That, there was no evidence to convict any of the accused persons and hence the revision application be rejected.

7] It is settled principles of law that power of revision under Section 397 and Section 401 of the Code are required to be read NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/63/2017 ORDER DATED: 15/02/2024 undefined together and Section 397 gives powers to the High Court to call for records as also exercise suo motu powers under Section 401 to examine the correctness, legality or propriety of any finding, sentence or order.
The main object is to set aright a patent defect of an error of jurisdiction or law or the perversity which has crept in the proceedings.

The revisional powers of the High Court are very wide but are purely discretionary and should be exercised only in rare cases to prevent miscarriage of justice where there is a glaring defect in procedure on points of law resulting in failure of justice.

8] Considering the submissions of the learned advocate for the respective parties and the order passed by the learned trial Court, it appears that the learned trial Court has sifted all materials placed in the charge-sheet and relied upon by the prosecution and has concluded that there is no sufficient material available that would satisfy the Court that the respondent has to be put for trial.

The learned Trial Court has discussed the evidence and found that there was no evidence that the respondent was at any time conducting the active business of the hotel and was sitting at the hotel and doing business.

That, even during the panchnama that were carried out, the respondent was not present and no person NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/63/2017 ORDER DATED: 15/02/2024 undefined had named the respondent in any manner.
That the respondent was added as an accused No. 7 only as he was the owner of the hotel, and merely on that basis, he could not be involved in the offence.

That, the learned Trial Court also recorded the findings that the prosecution could not show any evidence to put the respondent to trial or to connect the respondent in any manner with the offence and hence has allowed the application for discharge of the respondent from the offence as his role was attributed to the respondent in the charge sheet papers.
That, even otherwise, the final judgment in Sessions Case (POCSO) No. 147 of 2015 was pronounced by the learned Trial Court on 05 th May, 2022 and all the accused have been acquitted for the offence.

9] In view of the above, as learned Additional Public Prosecutor has not been able to show any illegality or impropriety in the order passed below Exhibit 4-J on 28 th September, 2016 in Sessions Case (POCSO) No. 147 of 2015 by the learned Special Judge (POCSO), City Civil & Sessions Court, Ahmedabad.and
